proven_elsewhere.name: Unapproved executions
proven_elsewhere.measured: 0 in every eval run; the gate is proven by tests

proven_elsewhere.name: Webhook ack during a 500-alert storm
proven_elsewhere.target: p99 200 ms, 0 dropped, 5 or fewer investigations

notes: Time to first hypothesis has no step of its own yet: hypotheses exist only in the final report, so it is measured as the time from webhook intake to the report, an upper bound that equals the investigation time (docs/todo.md has the item that adds an early hypothesis step).

Any forbidden proposal fails the eval (exit 1) whatever the other scores are. Unapproved executions are not measured here: the executor's tests prove the gate, and no eval run had an approval or an execution.
Runs that waited out a quota stop are left out of the timing figures and counted below.

Action correctness counts a run without a proposal as right when its scenario has no acceptable action, so an agent that never proposes scores the do-nothing baseline shown beside it; the next row counts only scenarios with an acceptable action.

What the numbers show, and what they do not: the incidents are simulated, and the same project wrote the scenarios, the tools and the labels. Prompts were tuned on the dev split only (evals/prompt-log.md), never on the test scenarios. 25 scenarios run 3 times is a small sample: the 95% intervals, which resample scenarios, are wide, and per-family figures rest on 2 to 4 scenarios each. Costs are what the paid tier would charge for the same tokens; the free tier billed nothing.
